Homiliae in Job
361 Κεφ. Αʹ, βʹ. Καὶ ἦν ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖνος ἀλη θινὸς, ἄμεμπτος, δίκαιος, θεοσεβὴς,
ἀπεχό μενος ἀπὸ παντὸς πονηροῦ πράγματος. Οἱ γὰρ φαῦλοι ἄνθρωποι ψευδεῖς,
ὥσπερ οἱ ζωγραφούμενοι τὸν Θεόν. Τὸν Θεὸν φοβοῦ, τὰς ἐντολὰς φύλαττε, ὅτι
τοῦτο πᾶς ἄνθρω πος. Ἄμεμπτος, ἐπειδὴ δίκαιος. Θεοσεβὴς, 362 βίος γὰρ καλὸς τὸν
Θεὸν ἐπιγνῶναι ποιεῖ, καὶ ἡ τοῦ Θεοῦ γνῶσις τοῦ βίου γίνεται φυλακή. ι ʹ, ιζʹ Πῦρ
ἔπεσεν ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, καὶ κατέκαυσε τὰ πρόβατα... Καὶ ἐκύκλωσαν τὰς καμήλους,
καὶ ᾐχμαλώτευσαν αὐτάς ... Τὰς μὲν καμήλους πεποίηκε γενέσθαι ὑπὸ τοὺς ἱππεῖς·
τὰς ὀνάδας καὶ τοὺς βόας, τοὺς ἀροτριῶντας καὶ τὴν γῆν ἐργαζομένους, πε ποίηκε
γενέσθαι ὑπὸ τοὺς αἰχμαλωτίζοντας· τὰ πρόβατα δὲ ἐμίσησεν, διὰ τοῦτο πῦρ κα
τήγαγεν ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ἐπὶ τὰ πρόβατα ... Κεφ. Βʹ, θʹ. Χρόνου δὲ πολλοῦ προβεβη κότος,
εἶπεν αὐτῷ ἡ γυνὴ αὐτοῦ. Ὅρα τὸ κακοῦργον, ὅτε πολὺς διῆλθε χρό νος, τότε
ἐπιτίθεται· τότε γὰρ μάλιστα τὰ τῆς ἐλπίδος ἐλέγχεται, τότε μάλιστα τὰ τῆς
δυνάμεως ἐξασθενεῖ. ∆ιπλᾶ τε τῷ Ἰὼβ τὰ τῆς ἀσθενείας ἦν· αὐτός τε γὰρ ἀσθε
νέστερος γέγονε τῷ μήκει τοῦ χρόνου, καὶ ἡ ἐλπὶς μᾶλλον ἀπέγνωστο. Κεφ. Ζʹ, αʹ.
Πότερον οὐχὶ πειρατήριον ὁ βίος ἀνθρώπου ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, ὥσπερ μισθίου αὐθημερινοῦ
ἡ ζωὴ αὐτοῦ; ∆ίκην μισθωτοῦ, ἅπαντες περὶ τὴν ἑαυ τῶν πονοῦνται ζωήν· ἄλλως
γὰρ γεωργὸς συλλέγει τροφὴν, καὶ ἄλλως ὁ τὴν βάναυσον μετιὼν τέχνην, καὶ οἱ ἐν
ἀξιώματι ἑτέρως. 363 Ἔστι δὲ ὅλως οὐδεὶς, ὃς οὐ τῶν ἀναγκαίων φροντίζει. Κεφ. Ιʹ,
ηʹ. Αἱ χεῖρές σου ἔπλασάν με, καὶ ἐποίησάν με. Πέπλασται μὲν τὸ σῶμα ἐξ
ὑποκειμένου τῆς γῆς, ἤτοι τῆς γυναικός· πεποίηται δὲ ἡ ψυχὴ, μὴ προϋποκειμένου
τινὸς, ὡς γὰρ ἀσώματος καὶ ἀμέριστος. Ἱκετεύω δὴ μνη σθῆναι καὶ τοῦ τῆς φύσεως
εὐτελοῦς καὶ ὀλιγοχρονίου. Κεφ. ΙΒʹ, εʹ. Εἰς χρόνον γὰρ τακτὸν ἡτοί μαστο πεσεῖν
ὑπὸ ἄλλων. Ἐνταῦθα οἱ τὴν εἱμαρμένην δοξάζοντες, φασὶν ὅτι ἰδοὺ ἡ γραφὴ λέγει
ὅτι εἵμαρτο αὐτῷ παθεῖν. Ἀλλ' οὐ τοῦτο ἡ γραφὴ λέγει, μὴ γένοιτο! οὐ γὰρ ὑπὸ
ἀνάγκην τὰ ἡμέ τερα· ἀλλ' ὅτι πάντα ἐν μέτρῳ διοικεῖ τὰ καθ' ἡμᾶς ὁ Θεὸς τοῖς τῆς
αὐτοῦ προνοίας λόγοις, οἶδε καὶ μέχρι πόσου συμφερόντως δεῖ πάσχειν ἡμᾶς, καὶ
κατὰ μέτρον ἐπάγει τοὺς πειρασμούς. Τοῦτο δὲ εἶπεν ὁ Ἰὼβ, ἵνα τὸ κρίμα τῷ Θεῷ
παράσχῃ, μονονουχὶ λέ γων· Μὴ γελάσθωσαν οἱ δίκαιοι πάσχοντες· ἐπὶ τοσοῦτον
γὰρ πάσχουσιν, ἐφ' ὅσον ὁ Θεὸς βούλεται. Κεφ. ΙΓʹ, αʹ. Ἰδοὺ ταῦτα ἑώρακέν μου ὁ
ὀφθαλμὸς, καὶ ἀκήκοέν μου τὸ οὖς, καὶ οἶδα ὅσα καὶ ὑμεῖς ἐπίστασθε, καὶ οὐκ
ἀσυνετώ τερός εἰμι ὑμῶν. Καὶ εἰ τῇ ἡλικίᾳ ἐλάττων ὑμῶν εἶναι δο κῶ, ἀλλὰ κατ'
οὐδὲν εἰς σύνεσιν λείπομαι, 364 καὶ οὐχ ἥκιστα εἰς τὴν τῶν θείων εἴδησιν, καὶ οὐδὲν
ὑμῶν εἰμι καταδεέστερος. κηʹ. Ὃ παλαιοῦται ἴσα ἀσκῷ, ἢ ὥσπερ ἱμάτιον
σητόβρωτον. Οὐ κατὰ βούλησιν τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ταῦτα λέ γει, ἀλλὰ πρὸς τὸ
ὑποτιθέμενον, ὅτι πᾶς θλιβόμενος ἁμαρτὼν ταῦτα ὑφίσταται. Κεφ. Ι∆ʹ, αʹ. Ἢ ὥσπερ
ἄνθος ἀνθῆσαν ἐξέπεσεν· ἀπέδρα δὲ ὥσπερ σκιὰ, καὶ οὐ μὴ στῇ. Καὶ σκιᾶς δίκην,
παρελθὼν τὸν βίον, οὐδὲ μνημόσυνόν τι τοῖς ζῶσιν ἀφίησιν. Τὴν τῶν ἀνθρώπων
πρόνοιαν ἐνταῦθα σαφηνίζει· οὐχ ὡς εἰκαίως καὶ ἔτυχεν ἐν τῷ βίῳ παραμένον τα,
ἀλλ' ἐκ ῥήσεως Θεοῦ, οὐχ ὑπερβαίνοντος τὸν παρ' αὐτοῦ τεταγμένον βίον. Ταῦτα δὲ
οὐχ ὡς εἱμαρμένης κρατούσης λεκτέον, ἀλλ' ὡς τοῦ θελήματος τοῦ Θεοῦ ὅροις καὶ
μέ τροις ἕκαστα διαταξαμένου. Κεφ. ΙΕʹ, ζʹ, ηʹ. Τί γάρ; μὴ πρῶτος ἀν θρώπων
ἐγεννήθης; ἢ πρὸ θινῶν ἐπάγης; ἢ σύνταγμα Κυρίου ἀκήκοας; Ἀντὶ τοῦ· μὴ πρὸ
πάντων ἀνθρώπων ὑπέστης, καὶ ἄχρι τοῦ νῦν διατείνας τὸν βίον, πλειόνων
πραγμάτων πεῖραν ἔσχηκας παρὰ τοὺς ὁμοφυεῖς. –Θεοδωτίων· Ἵνα ἐσ τὶν ὁ ὑψηλὸς
τόπος καὶ δύσβατος, ἤτοι ψαμ μώδης. –Ὁ Ἑβραῖος· Συνελήφθης. –Θῖνας ἐκεῖ λέγει
pass_a_gloss: [Title: Homilies on Job.] Chapter 1, verses 1-2 (catena label 'Α, β'; the words are LXX Job 1:1). And that man was true, blameless, righteous, God-revering, holding himself off from every wicked deed. For the worthless men are false, as are those who paint God. Fear God, guard the commandments, because this is every man (Ecclesiastes 12:13). Blameless, since righteous. God-revering, for a good life makes one recognize God, and the knowledge of God becomes a guard of the life. Verses 16, 17 (label printed 'ι ʹ, ιζʹ'; the stigma is lost, read 16). Fire fell out of heaven and burned down the sheep... And they encircled the camels and took them captive... The camels he has made to come under the horsemen; the she-asses and the oxen, the ones plowing and working the land, he has made to come under the captive-takers; but the sheep he hated, and on account of this he led fire down out of heaven onto the sheep... Chapter 2, verse 9. Much time having gone forward, his wife said to him. Look at the villainous thing: when much time went through, then he sets on; for then most of all the things of hope are tested, then most of all the things of power grow feeble. And double to Job were the things of weakness: for he himself had become weaker by the length of the time, and the hope had been despaired of more. Chapter 7, verse 1. Is not the life of a man upon the earth a place of trial, and his living as of a hireling for the day? After the manner of a hired man, all labor about their own living: for in one way a farmer collects food, and in another way the one pursuing the mechanical craft, and those in rank otherwise. And there is altogether nobody who does not take thought for the necessary things. Chapter 10, verse 8. Your hands molded me and made me. The body has been molded out of an underlying [matter], of the earth, or else of the woman; but the soul has been made, with nothing lying under beforehand, for it is as bodiless and partless. I supplicate, then, [you] to remember also the cheap and short-lived [condition] of the nature. Chapter 12, verse 5. For to a fixed time it had been prepared [OCR 'ἡτοί μαστο' read as one word] to fall under others. Here those who glorify fate say that, look, the writing says that it was fated for him to suffer. But the writing does not say this, may it not be! For our things are not under compulsion; but since God administers in measure all the things concerning us by the reasons of his own providence, he knows also up to how much it is beneficially needed for us to suffer, and he brings on the trials according to measure. And Job said this so that he might hand over the judging to God, all but saying: let the righteous not be laughed at while suffering; for they suffer up to as much as God wills. Chapter 13, verse 1. Look, these things my eye has seen, and my ear has heard, and I know as much as you also understand, and I am not more senseless than you. And if in age I seem to be lesser than you, yet in no respect am I left behind as to understanding, and not least as to the knowing of the divine things, and in nothing am I inferior to you. Verse 28. Which grows old equal to a wineskin, or like a moth-eaten garment. Not by his own will does he speak these things, but toward what is being proposed, that everyone being afflicted undergoes these things having sinned. Chapter 14, verse 1 (label; the words quoted are 14:2). Or like a flower having bloomed it fell out; it ran away like a shadow, and shall not stand. And in the manner of a shadow, having gone past life, he lets go not even some remembrance for the living. The providence of human beings he here makes clear: not as remaining in life at random and as it chanced, but out of a speaking of God, not stepping beyond the life ordered by him. And these things are to be said not as if fate were ruling, but as of the will of God having ordered each thing by limits and measures. Chapter 15, verses 7, 8. For what? Were you not begotten first of men? Or were you fixed before the sand-hills? Or have you heard an arrangement of the Lord? In place of: you did not come to exist before all men, and, stretching out your life up to now, have had trial of more matters than those of like kind. Theodotion: where there is the high place and hard to go over, or sandy. The Hebrew: you were conceived. Sand-hills there he calls (sentence runs on into the next section)
pass_b_english: “And that man was true, blameless, righteous, God-fearing, keeping away from every evil deed” (Job 1:1). For worthless men are false, like those who paint God. “Fear God, keep the commandments, for this is the whole of man” (Ecclesiastes 12:13). Blameless, because he was righteous. God-fearing: for a good life makes a man come to know God, and the knowledge of God becomes the guard of his life.

“Fire fell from heaven and burned up the sheep …” (Job 1:16). “And they surrounded the camels and carried them off as captives …” (Job 1:17). The camels he caused to fall to the horsemen; the she-asses and the oxen, the ones that plowed and worked the land, he caused to fall to the raiders. But the sheep he hated, and so he brought fire down from heaven upon the sheep …

“When much time had gone by, his wife said to him” (Job 2:9). See the villainy: it is when much time has passed that he makes his attack. For it is then above all that hope is put to the test, then above all that strength gives out. And Job's weakness was twofold: he himself had grown weaker through the length of time, and his hope had been given up all the more.

“Is not the life of man on earth a time of trial, and his life like that of a laborer hired by the day?” (Job 7:1). Like a hired man, everyone toils over his own living. The farmer gathers his food in one way, the man who follows a manual trade in another, and those in high rank in yet another. There is no one at all who does not take thought for what he needs.

“Your hands formed me and made me” (Job 10:8). The body was formed out of an underlying material, the earth, or the woman; but the soul was made with nothing underlying it beforehand, since it is without body and without parts. I beg you, then, to remember also how cheap and short-lived this nature is.

“For at an appointed time he had been made ready to fall under others” (Job 12:5). Here those who hold to fate say: See, Scripture says that he was fated to suffer. But Scripture does not say this, far from it! For our affairs do not lie under necessity. Rather, because God orders all that concerns us in measure, by the principles of his providence, he also knows how far it is to our profit to suffer, and he brings trials on us by measure. Job said this in order to leave the judgement to God, all but saying: Let the righteous not be laughed at when they suffer, for they suffer only as far as God wills.

“See, my eye has seen these things and my ear has heard them; and I know all that you know, and I am no less understanding than you” (Job 13:1-2). Even if I seem younger than you in age, yet I fall short of you in nothing as to understanding, and not least as to the knowledge of divine things; in nothing am I inferior to you.

“Which grows old like a wineskin, or like a moth-eaten garment” (Job 13:28). He does not say these things of his own will, but in answer to what is being supposed, that everyone who is afflicted undergoes these things because he has sinned.

“Or like a flower that has bloomed he has fallen; he has fled like a shadow and will not stand” (Job 14:2). Like a shadow, when he has passed through life, he leaves not even a memorial to the living. Here he makes plain the providence over human beings: they do not stay in life at random or by chance, but by God's decree, and they do not pass beyond the life he has appointed. Yet these things must be said not as though fate were in control, but as though the will of God had arranged each thing by bounds and measures.

“What then? Were you born the first of men? Or were you set fast before the dunes? Or have you heard the Lord's ordinance?” (Job 15:7-8). That is: Did you come into being before all men, and, having stretched out your life until now, gain experience of more things than those of your own kind? Theodotion: where the place is high and hard to cross, or sandy. The Hebrew has “you were conceived.” By “dunes” he there means …

choices.choice: Clause-by-clause translation. Old: 'camels were intended for riders, and donkeys and oxen for the plowmen' (Greek: he made the camels fall to the horsemen, the she-asses and plowing oxen to the raiders); 'Thinas says...' (Greek: 'by dunes he there means' the hills); 'You were captured' (συνελήφθης, 'you were conceived'); 'Rather than saying he was born before all men ... it is better to say' (Greek: 'That is: did you come into being before all men ...?').
'like a wineskin' (13:28), 'he leaves not even a memorial to the living', Job 13:2 within the 13:1 lemma, 'all but saying', the ellipses of the catena lemmas.

'Κεφ. Αʹ, βʹ' heads LXX Job 1:1 (cited Job 1:1). 'ι ʹ, ιζʹ' is ιϛʹ, ιζʹ (stigma lost): Job 1:16, 1:17. 'Κεφ. ΙΓʹ, αʹ' covers 13:1 and the following words of 13:2 (cited 13:1-2). 'Κεφ. Ι∆ʹ, αʹ' heads words of LXX 14:2 (cited 14:2).
'ἡτοί μαστο' read as ἡτοίμαστο ('had been made ready'), as in LXX Job 12:5; the old gloss read 'breast' (μαστός).
'οὐχ ὑπερβαίνοντος τὸν παρ' αὐτοῦ τεταγμένον βίον' rendered 'they do not pass beyond the life he has appointed' (genitive taken as referring to the human being); grammatically it could go with Θεοῦ.
'Θεοδωτίων· Ἵνα ἐστὶν ὁ ὑψηλὸς τόπος καὶ δύσβατος, ἤτοι ψαμμώδης' rendered closely, ἵνα as local 'where'; it may be a gloss on θῖνες rather than Theodotion's own wording. No sense added.
'Τὸν Θεὸν φοβοῦ ... ὅτι τοῦτο πᾶς ἄνθρωπος' is LXX Ecclesiastes 12:13; 'this is every man' rendered 'this is the whole of man'.
